top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock rests on a distinct, precisely stated idea, magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms in the Lamb-Dicke regime, which neither the 2005 comb prize nor the 2012 single-system prize contains. Its 10^-18 performance is verified by direct clock-to-clock comparison between independent laboratories, the two-name allocation (Katori for the concept and first strontium clock, Ye for the realisation at 10^-18 and many-body clock work) can be stated in the citation without a missing step, and the prize need not wait for the redefinition of the second. The Kane-Mele-Molenkamp prize is scientifically deep but leaves out the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal behind the HgTe experiment; magic-angle graphene is younger, with the pairing mechanism open and experimental credit narrower than the work. No award ranks last because the shortlist contains mature, verified achievements.
recusal_note: No direct connection to Katori or Ye is documented; I am a theorist in neighbouring atomic physics, and my documented collaborators (L'Huillier and the Lund group, Keller's ETH group, Schuch, Dahlstrom, Argenti, Indelicato) are not credited in any ranked proposal. Field proximity only; no recusal needed.
